newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola says momentum remains strong.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola says momentum remains strong.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises reported strong net earnings for the second quarter, helped along by acquisitions made in the previous year.

"Our momentum remains strong and our challenge for the rest of 1997 is to continue to effectively manage the price and volume equation in order to maximize operating results as we attempt to improve margins in the third quarter of 1997," said Henry Schimberg, president and chief operating officer of Coca-Cola Enterprises.
The company did say it was hurt by cooler weather and unfavorable currency transactions during the second quarter of 1997.

The company earned in 29 cents a share in the second quarter versus 15 cents a share in the same period a year ago. Second quarter revenues topped $2.9 billion versus $2.01 billion last year. Analyst earnings estimates for Coca-Cola Enterprises, compiled by First Call, forcast second quarter earnings of 25 cents a share.

There were some undermining factors mixed in with the good quarterly results. The cooler weather in the U.S. during the second quarter stymied volume increases to 3 percent compared to a 6-1/2 percent volume increase last year during that time, the company said.
European volume was flat compared to last year, the company said, also because of cool wet weather, mostly during the month of June.

Coca-Cola Enterprises is the sole licensed bottler for the Coca-Cola Co products in Belgium, Great Britain, the Netherlands, and most of France. It also distributes more than 58 percent of Coca-Cola's bottle and can volume in the United States
